issues.failure_explanation: With the definition [D(u)]_p = Δv^{-2} Σ_q (u_{p,q+1}-u_{p,q})^2 and λ_N equal to the first nonzero eigenvalue of the (1/Δv^2)-normalized Neumann Laplacian, the sharp discrete Poincaré inequality is D(u) ≥ (λ_N/Δv) ‖u-ū‖_v^{h,2} (equality holds for the first Neumann eigenmode, e.g., verified directly on a two-point grid). The displayed inequality D(u) ≥ λ_N‖u-ū‖_v^{h,2} is therefore false whenever Δv > 1, and, independently, it does not imply the proof's final combination: the dissipation identity equals (Δx/Δv)ΣM(Δu)^2 = ΔxΔv Σ_p M D(u), so the stated intermediate yields an extra factor Δv < 1; the final line requires the sharp 1/Δv factor. The two displayed steps are mutually inconsistent as written. The proposition's statement and the constant γ_h are nevertheless correct once the sharp inequality is used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the intermediate inequality with the sharp discrete Poincaré inequality D(u) ≥ (λ_N/Δv)‖u-ū‖_v^{h,2}; the remaining algebra then yields exactly the stated γ_h with no further changes.
issues.overall_effect: A displayed inequality and the subsequent combination step in the proof of Proposition 5.1 are invalid as written; the proposition's statement, the coercivity constant γ_h, and the downstream Theorem 5.1 (thm:main_AP) are unaffected.
issues.title: Discrete Poincaré step off by a factor of Δv in proof of Proposition 5.1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line insertion of the standard sharp Poincaré constant; the proposition's statement, γ_h, and Theorem 5.1 all survive unchanged, with no new lemma, construction, or replacement argument.

issues.failure_explanation: With the displayed three-point difference operators, β⊗T^(α) + β^{-1}⊗T^(1/α) assigns to f_{p,q+1} the coefficient Δv^{-2}(β_p α_{q+1/2} + β_p^{-1} α_{q+1/2}^{-1}) (and similarly wrong diagonal and f_{p,q-1} coefficients), whereas the actual stencil (3.7) has coefficient Δv^{-2}β_p α_{q+1/2} on f_{p,q+1} and Δv^{-2}β_p^{-1}α_{q-1/2}^{-1} on f_{p,q-1}. The identity is exact only for the one-sided operators (T̃^(α)w)_q = Δv^{-2}(α_{q+1/2}w_{q+1} - α_{q-1/2}w_q) and (T̃^(1/α)w)_q = Δv^{-2}(α_{q-1/2}^{-1}w_{q-1} - α_{q+1/2}^{-1}w_q), which are the operators actually appearing in the projection formulas of Section 3.2. Moreover, the claimed bound ‖T^(α)‖ ≤ 2α_max/Δv^2 is false for the displayed difference operator: it is a weighted Neumann Laplacian whose top eigenvalue approaches 4α_max/Δv^2 (sign-alternating trial functions localized where the slowly varying weights approach α_max give Rayleigh quotients exceeding 2α_max/Δv^2). The same bound does hold for the correct one-sided operators, so the proposition's statement and the constant κ_h survive.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the velocity operators as the one-sided operators dictated by stencil (3.7); the projection argument (using (I-P_X)(β̄h)=0 for h in ran(P_X)) and the induced-norm bounds via row/column sums then go through with the same constant κ_h, with boundary rows handled by the zero-flux ghost values.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition 5.2 establishes its estimate for an operator that is not L_h, using an induced-norm bound that fails for the displayed operators; the proposition's statement remains true, so Assumption 5.1 (asm:small_fluct) and Theorem 5.1 (thm:main_AP) are unaffected.
issues.title: False tensor-product decomposition and false induced-norm bounds in proof of Proposition 5.2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local rewrite of two displayed definitions plus elementary norm estimates that yield identical constants; the proposition's statement, κ_h, Assumption 5.1, and Theorem 5.1 all survive with no new nontrivial lemma or change to any claim.
